correctness.rationale: All graph distances are stated explicitly; a complete (S_n x S_n)-invariant decomposition of the (n^2+2n-1)-dimensional mean-zero space is reconstructed. At p=log_2(n/(n-1)), the paired standard blocks are negative definite, the mixed block is negative for n>=3, and the extra constant contrast is strictly negative by a rigorous lower bound on 3^p. The original A-versus-B contrast becomes positive for every larger p. The n=2 three-dimensional nullspace is handled separately. Centered Gram rank yields endpoint Euclidean dimensions. The associated checker directly builds finite cases; finite tests are not mistaken for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves whether subdividing each of n^2 edges of a natural extremal bipartite metric creates a new Schoenberg-positivity obstruction: it does not. A new exact endpoint embedding-rank law quantifies the n^2 new directions. Neither assertion follows from the old-vertex upper bound, and both are natural graph metric-invariance data relevant to finite positive-definite kernels.
